instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Basically Finished
cards.instruction: Describe incomplete, late, or improvised work as a thoughtful version of completion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Finished. I've left the cupboard shelves loose so you can practise the measuring I taught you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They fall down. There aren't any supports.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're finally checking underneath. It's a complete practice kit; you choose the heights around your tins.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I paid you to install it, not set homework. Here's the drill.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll finish one shelf for you to copy. A complete demonstration, with room for you to show what you learned.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The budget report is finished: a title page with space underneath. You remember my lesson about letting people contribute.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The board meets in ten minutes. They need your figures.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're thinking about the audience. This is the participation edition; they can put their figures straight in.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The chair wants your recommendation, not a worksheet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're finally distinguishing discussion from decision. I'll write 'Approve' under the title. Finished decision edition; no one has to fill anything in.

cards.title: I’ve Done This Before
cards.instruction: Perform calm familiarity with the task while learning how it works from every new clue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. I'll make your coffee. I know this machine: this button starts it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's steam. The coffee button is behind the flap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. Naturally. Steam first, then the concealed coffee controls. Where's your cup?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Here. It makes two cups unless you turn that dial.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Dial to one. I always tailor the standard procedure to the guest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. We'll have this tent up before the rain. I'm familiar with these sleeves.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: This one has clips. The poles cross first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. Yes, the clip system. Cross the poles; then we attach the fabric.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That fabric's the outer cover. We're standing on the inner tent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Step off the inner tent and we'll raise it first. I always lay everything out.

cards.title: Outdo the Effort
cards.instruction: Answer every favor, chore, or sacrifice with a bigger one that restores your lead.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Soup! You're finally using the recipe I taught you. I'll cook your dinners for a week in return.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're ill. I've already filled your freezer; please just rest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A whole freezer. Nearly as thorough as your teacher. When I'm better, I'll fill yours twice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's tiny. Just give the tubs back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the tubs. I'll bring a bigger freezer full of dinners. You always needed me to show you what a generous portion looks like.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thanks for the lift. My lessons in looking after people are finally paying off. I'll take your Saturday shift.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I already covered yours yesterday so you could rest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good initiative. I'll cover your whole weekend; you haven't overtaken your teacher yet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I swapped Sunday already so I could drive you to the airport.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll cancel the flight and cover your holiday. Watch how it's done: you can send your teacher a postcard from somewhere restful.

cards.title: Efficiency Win
cards.instruction: Celebrate each inconvenience as proof that a faster, cheaper, or smarter routine can now be invented.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The lift's broken! Finally, a use for the efficiency lessons I gave you. Cancel the gym; the stairs are included in our rent.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're eight floors up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you counted the repetitions. A complete workout on the way home—no separate trip.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What about carrying all the shopping?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent, you've added weights. Milk in one bag, tins in the other. Remember how I taught you to balance a load? We can stop paying to lift things now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The dishwasher's broken. Good: we'll serve curry in rolls. Remember my lesson about making one thing do two jobs?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've six rolls and twelve guests.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're finally checking portions before serving. Halve them: twelve open sandwiches and no plates to wash.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The curry will run off those flat halves.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent catch. Scoop the middle out of each half; stir the crumbs into the curry. Bowls and thickener—you've finally found a use for all that picking at bread.

cards.title: No Trouble at All
cards.instruction: Remain gracious and accommodating while making your growing inconvenience impossible to miss.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll carry your book bag. I taught you to keep a hand free for tickets; my shoulder can manage one more staircase.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Let me take it. There are dictionaries in there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Such a considerate offer. You're learning. Keep those tickets ready; I'll change shoulders at the bottom.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Our train's moved to platform twelve, across the bridge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, lead on. You remembered the board. Now find us a seat, like I showed you; these fingers will have earned a very long rest by then.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course your brother can stay for dinner. I taught you to welcome people; he can have my pie.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You haven't eaten either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How observant—you are learning to host. Don't worry about me; these peas will keep my plate occupied.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll order you a pizza. It takes forty minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Very thoughtful. You can practise keeping a hungry host company. Leave my fork out; I'll need it forty minutes after everyone else has finished.
